The card body proposes deciding `approvalsInbox.loadingMore`'s **en** value and `auth.device.loading`'s register *first*, and converging only afterwards. **Triage ruled otherwise at grading**, and that ruling is the one to implement.

## Adjudication (not re-litigable)

Triage, concentrated round 2026-08-25, on this card — `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task, `domain:ui`:

> Fix ruled at grading: converge each language pack to ONE rendering per language across the merged group, chosen by that pack's majority/most-idiomatic form (translation copy consistency, no contract change), and extend the #3878 census test to pin per-language uniformity for this group. Read the full thread at claim (one comment). If a language genuinely wants context-dependent variants, that is a fork — report, do not pick.

Two things follow, and the second is the one that matters:

1. The unit of work is the **whole merged 10-key group**, per language — ⛔ not the two keys #3880 originally named. A half-pass over the group is the failure this card was filed to prevent.
2. **The escape hatch is explicit and you are authorised to use it.** The card body argues that `approvalsInbox.loadingMore` (a *continuation* load, de `Lädt…`, ko `불러오는 중…`) and `auth.device.loading` (de `Lade…`, first person, on a device-pairing screen) may be **deliberately** different. If your measurement supports that, **report the fork — ⛔ do not pick**. Reporting it is a good run, not an incomplete one.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure them; your reading beats mine

Measured by the filer on `main` @ `2aff580b5`, and **not** re-verified by me on today's tree:

1. The group is exactly 10 keys whose `en` value is byte-identically `Loading…`. Re-derive it by flattening the packs and comparing exact values — ⛔ do not trust the card's table as the population. The group's membership is the whole basis of the ruling.
2. The tallies (de four renderings, ko two, ar two, six packs unanimous). ⚠️ The ar split is a **diacritic** difference (`جارٍ` vs `جاري`) on two keys — the card itself flags it as possibly a third, separate class. If it is, say so rather than folding it into the majority vote.
3. `#3878` converged all packs on U+2026 and there is now no ASCII `...` in any pack value, gated repo-wide by `ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts`. That test is your extension point — ⛔ do not weaken its existing assertions while adding the per-language uniformity pin.

⭐ The pin you add must be able to go red: a uniformity assertion that passes because it found nothing is the failure mode here. Assert the group is non-empty and has the expected membership before asserting uniformity over it.

## Fence

⛔ This is a **copy** change inside existing keys. Do not add or remove keys, do not touch `en` values (changing `approvalsInbox.loadingMore`'s en is the forked outcome, to be *reported*, not taken), and do not touch the glyph convergence.

## ACCEPT on substance — PR #6612. ⛔ Not enqueued yet: 5 checks still running, 0 failures.

`domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`, round 1. Reviewed against the diff, read myself.

### The three fence constraints, verified from the file list rather than the report

draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · `Fixes #5972` ✅ · **5 files**: changeset, the #3878 test file, and `locales/{ar,de,ko}.ts` ✅

- ⛔ **no `en` value touched** — `en.ts` **is not in the diff at all**, which is the strongest available form of that evidence, and `check:i18n-drift` independently prints `No en value changed in this range.`
- ⛔ **no key added or removed** — every change is a value edit on an existing line
- ⛔ **glyph convergence untouched** — every moved value keeps its U+2026

Nine values moved: de ×3, ko ×4, ar ×2. Each direction is the group majority **and** independently corroborated, which is the part that makes it a convergence rather than a vote: de's passive is the pack's dominant in-flight register (37 values), and ko reserves `불러오는 중` for strings that *name* the loaded object while the bare form is `로딩 중`.

### ⭐⭐⭐ It tested the card's hypothesis instead of deferring to it

I flagged two fork candidates and authorised reporting either. The delivery did something better than take the escape hatch: it **measured both, and they came out differently.**

**`approvalsInbox.loadingMore` — FALSIFIED, so it converged.** The card's theory was that a *continuation* load might want its own wording. Measurement, in both packs that could have shown it:
- de writes all four of that namespace's other in-flight states passively (`Wird genehmigt…`, `Wird abgelehnt…`, `Wird zurückgezogen…`, `Wird erneut eingereicht…`), so `Lädt…` **broke with its own neighbours** rather than marking anything;
- ko used the identical `불러오는 중…` on three plainly **initial** loads, so it cannot have been marking continuation either.

⭐ That is the right shape: the escape hatch was conditional on the measurement supporting it, and it did not. Converging there also *restores* the de namespace.

**`auth.device.loading` — SUPPORTED, so it was reported and not picked.** Filed as **#6611**.

### ⭐⭐ The `ar` split — exactly the trap I flagged, handled better than I asked

I warned that the ar pair might be "a third, separate class" and to say so rather than fold it into a majority vote. It is, and the account is precise: `جارٍ` and `جاري` are **one word in two orthographies** (the indefinite منقوص participle with tanwīn vs the yāʾ-retaining form), differing by a single code point — not two translations.

⭐ And the consequence was drawn correctly: **the split does not respect the group's boundary.** Pack-wide it is 92:8, and only 2 of those were in the group. So it converged the 2 the ruling covers and **filed the other 8 as #6610 rather than widening the fence** — the same move #3878 made when it fenced off the per-package fallback tables.

⭐ The count itself was measured with a Unicode-aware standalone-word match plus **positive and negative controls**, including the `التجارية` substring trap that an ASCII word-boundary regex falls straight into. That trap is exactly the false-zero family this lane keeps paying for.

### The pin can go red, and the waiver retires itself

Membership is asserted **before** uniformity — group derived from `en`, size and key set pinned by name, and every pack asserted to define all ten — so the rule cannot pass by matching nothing. Per-language non-vacuity counts too.

⭐ The fork exemption is the detail worth copying: it pins **both** the forked value **and that it still differs** from the converged rendering. Converge it later and the block goes red until the row is deleted — so the waiver cannot quietly outlive its reason. It also pins the two out-of-group keys (`approving` / `denying`) that are the fork's whole justification, so if *they* move the fork stops being justified.

Ablation, 3 legs, all predicted-red / observed-red. ⭐ Leg B predicted a membership failure and got that **plus** an unpredicted second diagnostic — reported rather than smoothed.

⭐ The sanitizer self-check was **measured, not asserted**: the body contains zero angle-bracket characters, so there was nothing for the sanitizer to eat. That is a real answer to the question rather than a glance.

### The two open questions — one is mine, one is not

**`approvalsInbox.loadingMore`'s `en` value: option A, leave it. Ruled here.** Declining a speculative change is this seat's call, and the measurement above retired the question rather than deferring it — no pack showed evidence any translator read that key as semantically different. B would be a 10-value churn plus a pin edit to encode a distinction the product does not make. ⛔ Not escalating something measurement has already answered.

**The de `auth.device` register: correctly NOT taken here, and correctly filed.** It is copy voice over keys this card does not fence in. #6611 is its home and triage routes it from there — I am not ruling it and not putting it in the maintainer's inbox myself.

⚠️ One finding inside it deserves to survive the routing: **`Ablehne…` is not a grammatical German form.** `ablehnen` is a separable-prefix verb, so the first person is *ich lehne ab* → `Lehne ab…`. That does not settle the register question, but it substantially weakens the "the first person was deliberate" reading, and it means **whichever way #6611 goes, `Ablehne…` should not survive**.

### Housekeeping

⭐ `skip-changeset` correctly **not** applied, with the reason stated: it is a phantom label in this repo (nothing reads it), so applying it would only mint a false status. That matches this lane's standing note and was worth saying rather than silently skipping.

Both out-of-scope findings verified present by me: **#6610** (unlabelled — a specific normalisation for triage to grade) and **#6611** (unlabelled). ⭐ #6610 bounds its own claim honestly — it asks for an Arabic reader to confirm the direction, and says plainly that the indefinite-participle judgement "is a reading, not a measurement."
